candidates.requirement: Exercise mapping with both UTF8PROC_CHARBOUND and UTF8PROC_STRIPCC so retained grapheme markers and removal of boundaries before stripped controls are reachable.
candidates.target_route: A valid NUL-terminated input reaches utf8proc_map; mapping decomposes it, normalizes the UTF-32 buffer, then encodes grapheme markers.
candidates.failure_condition: The harness never passes both options in one mapping call. Its direct normalization calls omit CHARBOUND, so they cannot exercise removal of a boundary created by decomposition.
candidates.alternative_paths: The normalization shortcuts omit STRIPCC. Separate harness calls do not pass one call's output into another. Natural input cannot add an option flag.

before.requirement: The same retained-marker and boundary-removal capability was not available: STRIPCC removed negative boundary sentinels, and there was no branch to remove a boundary preceding a stripped control.
before.reason: The old source accepted the option combination but could not produce this specific behavior. The absence of the new regression test alone is not the basis for this assessment.

after.requirement: Mapping a valid control-containing string with CHARBOUND|STRIPCC must retain markers for surviving graphemes and remove the boundary before a stripped control.
after.reason: Normalization now retains negative sentinels and removes a preceding boundary when it strips a control with CHARBOUND selected. The old harness never selects both flags.

claims.reason: The obligation is the same combined-option output capability on both sides. Before, the old implementation removed its marker sentinels; after, the capability exists but the fixed harness options block coverage.
